settings.heading: Method 1: The String or Paper Strip Trick
settings.body: This is the simplest way to measure at home. You'll need a piece of string, dental floss, or a thin strip of paper, plus a ruler and a pen.
settings.list_items: Wrap: Wrap the string or paper strip snugly around the base of the finger you want to size, where a ring would normally sit. Mark: Use a pen to mark the point where the string overlaps to form a complete circle. Measure: Lay the string flat and measure the length from the start to the mark, in millimetres — this is your finger's circumference. Convert: Compare that measurement against a ring size conversion chart, or bring it to us in-store and we'll convert it for you on the spot.

settings.heading: Method 2: Measure a Ring You Already Own
settings.body: If you already own a ring that fits the intended finger comfortably, you can measure that instead — it's often more accurate than measuring the finger directly, since fingers can swell slightly throughout the day.
settings.list_items: Choose the right ring: Pick one that's worn on the same finger you're sizing for — sizes can vary slightly between hands and fingers. Measure the inside diameter: Place the ring on a ruler and measure straight across the inside edge, in millimetres. Or trace it: Draw around the inside of the ring on paper, then measure the diameter of the circle you've drawn. Double-check: Measure a couple of times to make sure your figure is consistent before converting to a ring size.

settings.heading: Ring Size Conversion Chart
settings.body: Once you have your finger's circumference or your ring's inside diameter in millimetres, use the table below as a guide to your Australian, UK, US and EU size.
settings.list_items: AU/UK H — US 4 — EU 46: 14.6mm diameter, 45.9mm circumference AU/UK J½ — US 5 — EU 49: 15.7mm diameter, 49.3mm circumference AU/UK L — US 6 — EU 51: 16.5mm diameter, 51.9mm circumference AU/UK N — US 6½ — EU 52: 16.9mm diameter, 53.1mm circumference AU/UK N½ — US 7 — EU 54: 17.3mm diameter, 54.4mm circumference AU/UK P½ — US 8 — EU 57: 18.2mm diameter, 57.2mm circumference AU/UK R½ — US 9 — EU 59: 19.0mm diameter, 59.5mm circumference AU/UK T½ — US 10 — EU 62: 19.8mm diameter, 62.1mm circumference

settings.heading: Tips for an Accurate Measurement
settings.list_items: Measure at the end of the day: Fingers are naturally slightly larger in the evening and in warm weather, which gives a more realistic everyday fit. Avoid measuring cold hands: Fingers shrink in the cold, which can lead to a ring that's too tight later. Consider the band width: Wider bands generally need to be slightly larger than a thin band to fit comfortably over the knuckle. Mind the knuckle: Your knuckle is usually larger than the base of your finger — the ring needs to pass over it, then sit comfortably below. Measure the correct hand: Your dominant hand is often slightly larger than the other, so always measure the exact finger the ring will be worn on.

settings.heading: Still Not Sure? We'll Size It for You
settings.body: At-home methods are a reliable starting point, but nothing beats a professional fitting. Bring the finger — or the ring — in-store and our team will confirm the exact size in a couple of minutes, free of charge.
